featured_reviews.name: Sushmita Mohite
featured_reviews.review_text:
Panshikar had been on my list for its reputation for Maharashtrian snacks, and I finally visited yesterday evening. Conveniently located just outside Dadar railway station, I was eager to try their specialties.
I started with the Misal Pav, which wasn't quite my style due to the farsan, poha, and batatyachi bhaji making it a bit soggy. However, the taste was decent, though slightly on the sweeter side.
Next, I tried the Bhajani Thalipeet it was deep-fried and tasted good, paired with their lasun chutney, which was absolutely delicious.
The star of the evening, however, was the Kothimbir Vadi. It was perfectly cooked—crispy on the outside and soft on the inside, making it an absolute treat.
I ended the meal with Piyush which is a must-try and a great way to conclude the meal.
Overall, the experience was good. The service was fast and efficient, and I appreciated the quick turnaround. A heads-up: Panshikar is closed on Sundays.
If you're in the mood for some classic Maharashtrian snacks, this is definitely worth a visit!

featured_reviews.name: SHUBHAM KALE
featured_reviews.review_text:
Panshikar & Co., established in 1931, stands as a true symbol of Mumbai’s old-world Maharashtrian charm. The moment you step in, you’re greeted with a nostalgic warmth — simple décor, authentic aromas, and that unmistakable traditional touch that feels like home.

The menu brings forth classic Maharashtrian dishes — from fluffy thalipeeth and misal to melt-in-the-mouth modaks and sabudana vada, each dish reflects the purity and simplicity of traditional cooking. The flavors are rich, authentic, and prepared with the kind of care that only a legacy eatery can offer.

Yes, the prices are a bit on the higher side, especially compared to the regular local joints, but considering the heritage, quality, and authenticity they maintain, it’s worth every rupee.

Panshikar & Co. isn’t just about food — it’s an experience that connects you to the roots of Maharashtra, one bite at a time.

3/5 Stars –
Decent Vada Pav Spot in the Busy Lane
Visited Aakash The Sweet Corner recently and ordered a huge quantity of Vada Pav for the family (around 15-20 pieces). They handled the bulk order without any fuss even during the evening rush.

The vada pav itself was pretty good – fresh, hot, and the vada was nicely crispy with a soft potato filling. The chutneys were the real highlight; the green chutney was properly spicy and packed a good punch, which made each bite quite satisfying. The quantity was generous and the price felt reasonable for the area.

That said, it’s a typical busy street-side joint – no seating, very crowded, and service is quick but a bit chaotic. Hygiene is average (what you’d expect in such a market setup).

Overall, a solid choice if you’re craving spicy, no-nonsense vada pav in Connaught Place/Paharganj area. Worth a visit if you’re in the mood for street food, but nothing extraordinary either. 3 stars from me.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Dadar Surti Farsan Mart is one of those places that every foodie in Mumbai has strong opinions about, and after trying them, I can finally see why. I stopped by recently to grab a quick snack, and here is my honest take on the experience.

The Food (The Star of the Show):
Let's get straight to the point—their samosa is exceptional. The outer shell is perfectly crisp and flaky, not too thick, and shatters beautifully when you bite into it. The filling inside is well-spiced and flavorful without being too greasy. But what truly elevates the entire experience is their chutney. It is an absolute game-changer. It strikes that perfect balance between sweet, tangy, and spicy, complementing the samosa so well that you will find yourself asking for extra portions. If you are a samosa connoisseur, this is a must-try.

The Vibe & Service:
Being a farsan mart, it operates with that classic "counter-service" efficiency. It can get quite crowded, especially during evening snack time, so be prepared to wait a few minutes to place your order. The staff is efficient, though they are clearly accustomed to the rush.

The Price Factor:
Now, onto the one point that keeps this from being a perfect 5-star review for me: the pricing. There is no denying that the quality is top-tier, but the cost is undeniably on the higher side compared to your average local snack joint. You are paying a premium for the brand name and the location. While the taste justifies the splurge occasionally, it is the kind of place you go to when you want a "treat yourself" snack rather than an everyday cheap eat.

Verdict:
If you love samosas and want to taste one of the best versions available in Mumbai, you have to visit Dadar Surti Farsan Mart. Just go in knowing that your wallet will feel a slightly lighter for the experience

On a rainy Sunday, I visited Dadar Surti Farsan, a well-known spot for traditional Gujarati snacks, and the experience was absolutely delightful. The drizzle outside made it the perfect day to indulge in some hot and savory farsan, and this place did not disappoint. The shop has a simple, no-fuss vibe, but what truly stands out is the freshness and authenticity of the food served.

I began with their **soft and spongy dhokla**, which was perfectly steamed, light on the stomach, and mildly tangy with just the right hint of sweetness. Topped with mustard seeds and curry leaves, it had that authentic Gujarati touch. Next, I tried the makai roll, which was both unique and flavorful. The subtle sweetness of corn paired with the spices made it a wholesome snack and something I’d definitely go back for.

The highlight for me, however, was the pyaz kachori. Crispy on the outside and generously stuffed with a spicy onion mixture inside, it was comfort food at its best—especially when enjoyed hot on a rainy day. Each bite was bursting with flavor and paired perfectly with the chutneys served alongside.

One of the best parts about Dadar Surti Farsan is its **reasonable pricing**. Despite the quality and freshness of the items, the rates are pocket-friendly, making it a great place for both quick bites and takeaway parcels. The staff was quick and efficient, ensuring customers didn’t have to wait long even though the place was quite busy.

Overall, my visit to Dadar Surti Farsan was an enjoyable mix of great taste, tradition, and value for money. For anyone who enjoys authentic Gujarati snacks, this place is a must-try and the experience becomes even more special when savored on a rainy day.

featured_reviews.name: Gurvinder Pal Singh Kalra
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently ordered from Purshottamm Kandoi Haribhai Damodar Mithaiwala (what a legendary name for a legendary place!) to celebrate the fantastic victory of Mrs. Sheetal Gambhir in the recent BMC elections. As a proud supporter, I wanted something special, authentic, and indulgent to mark the occasion, and this iconic Mumbai sweet shop (since 1952!) delivered beyond expectations. I gave it a perfect 5-star rating on the app, and here’s why it truly deserves every bit of it.
The order included:
•	Vati Dhokla (those fluffy, perfectly steamed yellow cubes with the classic tempering of mustard seeds, curry leaves, and green chilies – soft, spongy, and bursting with tangy flavor)
•	Kothimbir Wadi (fresh, herby coriander-packed slices that were crispy outside and moist inside – a Gujarati classic done to perfection)
•	Healthy Cutlets (surprisingly delicious, packed with nuts and veggies, great texture, and a guilt-free snack option)
•	And the absolute star of the show – Kesar Rasmalai (12 pieces)!
Oh, the Kesar Rasmalai was pure bliss! The spongy chenna balls were soaked just right in thick, creamy, saffron-infused milk – not overly sweet, beautifully aromatic with real kesar strands, and topped with nuts for that premium touch. Each bite melted in the mouth, and the subtle cardamom flavor made it feel luxurious yet comforting. It was hands-down the best rasmalai I’ve had in a long time – fresh, rich, and so delicately balanced.
We enjoyed this delightful spread together at Smartflex Gym (shoutout to the amazing vibe there in Dadar West!), turning our post-workout session into a mini celebration feast. Sharing these treats with friends after a good sweat felt extra rewarding – the savory snacks fueled us perfectly, and the rasmalai was the ultimate sweet victory reward. Everything arrived fresh, well-packaged, and piping hot/cold as needed.
Purshottamm never disappoints with their authentic Gujarati flavors and consistent quality. This order was a complete winner – tasty, hygienic, timely delivery, and full of joy. Highly recommended for any celebration (or just because!). If you’re in Mumbai and craving genuine mithai and farsan, this is the place.
Thank you, Purshottamm, for making our celebration even sweeter! 🏆🍯✨
5/5 stars – will order again and again!

Time tested. Been tasting their wonderful offerings over time.. to be precise, relishing since 1972 and still cant have enuf of their supremely crafted “Petha Barfi”.
